newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cenbank raises discount rate as crown floats.
newsitem.headline: Czech cenbank raises discount rate as crown floats.

text.p: The Czech National Bank, which earlier said it would float the Czech crown beginning on Tuesday, raised its key discount lending rate on Monday to 13 percent from 10.5 percent.

In a statement, central bank spokesman Martin Svehla said that the bank would keep for the near future its last-resort Lombard rate at 50 percent. The CNB raised the Lombard rate to that level in an effort to cut off speculative short selling of the crown in the last 10 days.

The statement said the central bank would further adjust its repo rates which regulate liquidity on the money market in line with market conditions, but it expected that rates would fall in the short term as the money market stabilised.
The average yield on the central bank's one-day repo operation on Monday was 72.37 percent, while a one-week repo yielded an average of 74.84 percent.

"In a horizon of months" the bank said it expected crown to stabilise in a range of between 17 to 19.5 to the mark. The crown was fixed on Monday at 18.078 to the mark and was trading at 18.066 after the central bank's announcements.

"The change of the exchange rate policy is strengthening the relationship of the crown and mark and it is creating room for movement of the exchange rate on levels which will contribute to a lowering of the external imbalances," the statement said.
The crown has come under pressure in the last 10 days amid investor concern at swelling current account and foreign trade deficits and a slowdown in economic growth.

"The aim is to gradually create conditions for improvement in the development of the current account of the balance of payments, stabilising of the currency and in the long-term for more-balanced growth of the Czech economy," the statement said.
